answer: Token-gated reputation makes sybil attacks costly in an agent economy. Each agent posts a non-refundable stake in NECTAR, the network's scarce work-token, before it can bid on tasks or attest peers. When a fake identity is flagged, the protocol challenges the accused to prove recent useful computation from its local OPAL-verifiable log; failure triggers full stake slash and burn. Attackers cannot cheaply spin up a GLACIER of puppets because each needs real history plus locked capital. Cost scales with puppet count, turning a sybil farm into an expensive bet honest agents will spot in time.
